headline: 2,200-person relocatable camp
story: Weatherhaven supplied Relocatable Temporary Camp (RTC) assets for 2,200 personnel supporting NATO operations in Afghanistan — MTS Lite sleeper shelters, Series 4 dining and storage facilities, MEX-26 aircraft and vehicle maintenance shelters, and MECC ablution and laundry units.

headline: UNAVEM II, 1992
story: In 1992, Weatherhaven deployed 45 five-person turnkey, air-conditioned camps in Angola for the UN peacekeeping mission UNAVEM II. Series 4 shelters provided sleeping quarters, kitchens, dining, offices, assembly halls and ablutions.

headline: Series 4 shop, 30 years in use
story: Weatherhaven provided Series 4 shelters as workforce housing while Concordia Station was being built. Once construction was complete, the shelters stayed in place as overflow accommodation for polar researchers during the summer season. A 22-foot-wide Series 4 shop has been up and in continuous use at Concordia for 30 years.

headline: Troll Airfield
story: The Norwegian Polar Institute purchased a Weatherhaven MECC shelter for Troll Airfield, the busiest airfield in East Antarctica. The MECC serves as the air traffic control centre and as a refuge during bad weather.

headline: UNAMID police camp, 2009
story: In 2009, Weatherhaven supplied 150-person camps to support Formed Police Units deployed to UNAMID, the joint African Union–UN peacekeeping mission in Darfur. This was one of three such camps.

headline: UNTAC, 1993
story: In 1993, Weatherhaven supplied peacekeeping camps for UNTAC in Cambodia: two 500-person camps and one 160-person camp, each fully equipped with sleepers, kitchen, dining, office, assembly hall and ablution facilities.

headline: Accommodation shelters, 1999
story: In 1999, Weatherhaven delivered 60 accommodation shelters for UN operations in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. In 2012, the shelters’ barrel covers were replaced.

headline: 44-person exploration camp
story: Fortescue purchased a turnkey 44-person camp for its copper exploration site in southwestern Ecuador. Scope of supply included shelters, furnishings, electrical and mechanical systems, food prep and storage equipment, and site distribution of power, waste and potable water. The site was accessible only by air — or an eight-hour hike up a dry creek bed.

headline: UNMEE, 2000
story: In 2000, Weatherhaven supported the UN peacekeeping mission UNMEE, a joint Netherlands–Canada deployment, with the Canadian Armed Forces operating from 250-person relocatable temporary camps.

headline: Mineral exploration camps
story: Weatherhaven has supplied turnkey camps of various sizes to support mineral exploration across French Guiana. Most sites were accessible only by air or upriver.

headline: 40-person turnkey camp
story: Weatherhaven supplied a 40-person turnkey camp to Ironbark Zinc at Citronen Fjord in northern Greenland, including shelters, mechanical and electrical systems, power generation, furnishings, and food prep and storage equipment. At the time, it was the northernmost workforce camp in the world.

headline: MINUGUA
story: Weatherhaven supplied a peacekeeping camp for MINUGUA, the UN mission in Guatemala, including Series 4 sleeper shelters and ablution facilities.

headline: Simandou iron ore project
story: Weatherhaven played an integral role in developing the Simandou iron mine in southeastern Guinea — the largest undeveloped iron ore deposit in the world at the time. Weatherhaven camps supported exploration, construction of the rail line connecting the mine to the port at Conakry, and construction of the mine itself. A number of Weatherhaven camps were also used by Doctors Without Borders during the 2014 Ebola outbreak.

headline: Gold exploration camps
story: Weatherhaven Series 8 Tropical Model shelters were used by mineral exploration companies from around the world to delineate major gold deposits in Guyana. Customers included the Government of Guyana itself.

headline: Disaster relief, 2010
story: In 2010, Weatherhaven supplied 112 MTS-3 shelters, in 16' x 16' and 20' x 18' sizes, for disaster relief in Haiti.

headline: UNOSOM, Somalia
story: Weatherhaven supplied a 90-person turnkey camp of insulated Series 4 structures to the Irish Defence Forces for the UN mission UNOSOM in Somalia.

headline: Kobe earthquake response
story: After the 1995 Kobe earthquake, Japan’s Self-Defense Forces purchased 94 MECC shelters for their emergency response teams (1995–96). Each shelter was fitted with a sink, shower and built-in bagging toilet and delivered with complete operations and maintenance manuals. Once deployed, the shelters served as triage centres or command posts.

headline: MEX-26 shelters
story: Weatherhaven supplied two MEX-26 shelters to Jordan.

headline: Copper project workforce housing
story: Weatherhaven Series 4 insulated shelters are in use as workforce housing in the high steppes of Kazakhstan, at one of the largest undeveloped copper deposits in the world.

headline: KOPRI Antarctic program
story: KOPRI, the Korea Polar Research Institute, purchased Polarhaven and Endurance shelters for deep-field operations near Jang Bogo Station at Terra Nova Bay, Antarctica.

headline: KFOR
story: Weatherhaven supplied 1,000-person Relocatable Temporary Camps (RTC) for the NATO-led KFOR peacekeeping mission in Kosovo, combining Series 4, MEX-26, MECC and MTS shelters.

headline: UNIKOM, 1991
story: In 1991, Weatherhaven supplied a peacekeeping camp for UNIKOM, the UN Iraq–Kuwait Observation Mission, including sleepers, kitchen, dining, office, assembly hall and ablutions.

headline: UNIFIL, 1991
story: In 1991, Weatherhaven supplied a 20-person camp of Series 8 shelters to UNIFIL, the UN peacekeeping mission in Lebanon, including sleepers, kitchen, dining, office, assembly hall and ablutions.

headline: Diamond exploration
story: Weatherhaven Series 4 shelters supported diamond exploration in Lesotho.

headline: Wind-rated turnkey camps
story: Weatherhaven supplied insulated Series 4 turnkey camps to the Marshall Islands, fitted with additional anchoring and wind kit systems.

headline: MINURSO to COVID-19
story: Weatherhaven’s work in Mauritania spans three decades: 18 UN peacekeeping camps for MINURSO in 1992, including sleepers, kitchens, dining, offices, assembly halls and ablutions; three 8-person dormitories and miscellaneous equipment in 2003; and a 100-bed COVID-19 field hospital in 2020.

headline: Reynosa workforce camp
story: Weatherhaven supplied a commercial workforce camp built from insulated Series 4 shelters in Reynosa, Mexico.

headline: Mexican Navy disaster response
story: Weatherhaven supplied four ATEPS shelters, through Unimog, for a Mexican Navy disaster response camp — housing a kitchen, command post, ablutions and a medical clinic.

headline: Oyu Tolgoi copper complex
story: Weatherhaven Series 4 structures housed the workforce through both the exploration and mine development phases at the Oyu Tolgoi copper complex in the Gobi Desert. At one time the site had two of the largest core shacks at any exploration site in the world — both built from Series 4 shelters.

headline: ONUMOZ, 1993
story: In 1993, Weatherhaven supplied a peacekeeping camp of 294 Series 6 tropical shelters for ONUMOZ, the UN operation in Mozambique.

headline: Everest Base Camp
story: Weatherhaven Endurance shelters have been used at Everest Base Camp.

headline: 35+ years with Antarctica NZ
story: The New Zealand Antarctic Programme and its successor, Antarctica New Zealand, have been Weatherhaven customers for more than 35 years, purchasing Polarhaven, Endurance and Series 4 shelters.

headline: ORF documentary film crew
story: ORF, Austria’s national broadcaster, relied on Weatherhaven to house its film crew while filming a documentary about the discovery of Franz Josef Land.

headline: PNG LNG and Wafi-Golpu
story: There may be more Weatherhaven structures per square kilometre in Papua New Guinea than anywhere else on earth. Projects include the PNG LNG pipeline, the Wafi-Golpu gold deposit, LNG drill sites near Lake Kutubu and many more. Customers include Spiecapag, Barrick Gold, Newmont, ExxonMobil and countless junior mining companies.

headline: Police command centre
story: The Singapore Police Force purchased a MECC shelter for use as a command centre.

headline: UNMISS
story: Through a long-term supply agreement between Weatherhaven and the UN Procurement Division, the UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) purchased MECC shelters for command posts and troop accommodation near Juba.

headline: 112-bed BHP camp
story: Weatherhaven designed, built, transported and constructed a 112-bed turnkey workforce camp for BHP at its bauxite exploration site in western Suriname. Scope of supply included shelters, furnishings, mechanical and electrical kits, food prep and storage equipment, and site services including power distribution, wastewater collection and potable water supply.

headline: Turnkey peacekeeping camp
story: Weatherhaven supplied a peacekeeping camp including sleepers, ablutions, laundry, kitchen, dining, water treatment, office modules and meeting rooms.
